what_worked: Exceptional framing of data-quality limitations and the anonymized-revenue blind spot as a genuine strategic finding.
fix_next: The deck consistently uses MRR instead of 30-day revenue, producing wrong totals ($13.47M vs $15.6M) and cascading percentage errors throughout.
verdict: Strong narrative and honest framing undermined by using the wrong revenue field.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2/4: Total reported as $13.47M using MRR field; frozen dataset total 30-day revenue is $15,596,344.59 — the entire deck's denominator is wrong. Slide 2: Top-10 share stated as 48%; reference is 49.6%. Slide 2: Zero-revenue count 197 (19.7%); reference shows 216 (21.6%). Slide 2: B2B/B2C median multiple stated as 5.7x ($1,036/$181); reference medians give ~2.35x. Slide 2: Anonymous share stated as 26.5% and 28% interchangeably; reference is 26.525% of revenue but anonymous count is 129/1000=12.9% of companies — the 28.1% on slide 11 conflicts with 26.5% on slide 2.

evidence.insight: Slide 9 correlation table distinguishing vanity metrics from real revenue drivers is genuinely useful; the blind-spot framing (56.5% uncategorized MRR) is an original and decision-relevant observation; domain-rating tier analysis on slide 7 adds depth.
evidence.narrative: Clear thesis introduced on slide 2 ('power-law market hiding a blind spot'), carried through concentration (slide 5), data quality (slide 6), comparative signals (slide 7), synthesis (slide 9), recommendations (slide 10), limitations (slide 11), and a tight three-point close (slide 12). Purposeful sequence with a real landing.
evidence.framing: Slide 3 explicitly states assumptions, defines MRR, justifies median over mean, flags no time series, and explains missing-data handling. Slide 11 dedicates a full page to limitations. Causal disclaimers on slides 7 and 9. Audience clearly identified. Exceptionally transparent for student work.
evidence.accuracy: The deck uses mrr_usd rather than 30-day revenue as its base metric, producing a total of $13.47M vs the reference $15.6M. This cascades: top-10 share, zero-revenue count, B2B/B2C multiplier (5.7x vs ~2.35x), and anonymous revenue share all deviate materially from the frozen reference. The MRR tier histogram bins sum to 1000 which is internally consistent but built on the wrong field.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/gold palette, clear hierarchy with section labels, well-labeled axes, appropriate chart types (horizontal bar for top 10, bar charts for distributions, pie for category share). Pie chart on slide 8 is acceptable but not ideal for 7 categories. No chart junk. Slightly template-heavy but functional and legible throughout.
evidence.ai_slop: Mild consulting-speak in headers ('Executive Performance Review', 'Deep Dive') but content is substantive and dataset-specific throughout. No decorative-but-meaningless graphics. No filler slides. Not slop.
